nl_statement: Prove that $\frac{(x+2)^p-2^p}{x}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.
nl_proof: $\frac{(x+2)^p-2^p}{x} \quad \quad p$ is on add pprime $Z[x]$ $$ \frac{(x+2)^p-2^p}{x} \quad \text { as a polynomial we expand }(x+2)^p $$ $2^p$ cancels with $-2^p$, every remaining term has $x$ as $a$ factor $$ \begin{aligned} & x^{p-1}+2\left(\begin{array}{l} p \\ 1 \end{array}\right) x^{p-2}+2^2\left(\begin{array}{l} p \\ 2 \end{array}\right) x^{p-3}+\ldots+2^{p-1}\left(\begin{array}{c} p \\ p-1 \end{array}\right) \\ & 2^k\left(\begin{array}{l} p \\ k \end{array}\right) x^{p-k-1}=2^k \cdot p \cdot(p-1) \ldots(p-k-1), \quad 0
